claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately conveys the prohibition in paragraph (a)(1) barring a driver from using alcohol or being under the influence within 4 hours prior to going on duty, operating, or having physical control of a commercial motor vehicle.

The claim accurately reproduces the prohibition in paragraph (a)(2) barring alcohol use, being under the influence, or having any measured alcohol concentration or detected presence while on duty, operating, or in physical control of a commercial motor vehicle.

The claim fully captures paragraph (a)(3), including the core prohibition against possessing qualifying wine, beer, or distilled spirits while on duty or operating a commercial motor vehicle, alongside both statutory exceptions for manifested shipments and bus passengers.
The claim accurately represents paragraph (b)(1), prohibiting motor carriers from requiring or permitting a driver to violate any provision of paragraph (a).

The claim faithfully reflects paragraph (b)(2), prohibiting motor carriers from requiring or permitting a driver to be on duty or operate a CMV if the driver appears to have used alcohol within the preceding 4 hours based on appearance, conduct, or other substantiating evidence.
The claim accurately conveys paragraph (c), requiring that any driver found in violation of paragraph (a) or (b) be placed out of service immediately for 24 hours.
The claim correctly reflects paragraph (c)(1), specifying that the 24-hour out-of-service period begins upon the issuance of an out-of-service order.
The claim accurately captures paragraph (c)(2), prohibiting drivers from violating the terms of an out-of-service order issued under this section.
The claim accurately reflects the requirement under paragraph (d)(1) that a driver issued an out-of-service order must report its issuance to his or her employer within 24 hours.

The claim comprehensively captures paragraph (d)(2), including the 30-day reporting requirement to the designated State official, the exception when review is requested, and the reporting timeline following affirmation.

The claim accurately states the initial petition mechanism in paragraph (e), permitting a driver subject to an out-of-service order to submit a written petition for review within 10 days to the Division Administrator or State Director.
The claim accurately states the authority granted to the Division Administrator or State Director in paragraph (e) to affirm or reverse the out-of-service order.
The claim accurately states the secondary review provision in paragraph (e), allowing any driver adversely affected by such order to petition the Administrator for review under 49 CFR 386.13.

unit_judgments.rationale: C0000 covers the complete prohibition against pre-duty/operating alcohol use or being under the influence within 4 hours.
C0001 completely covers the prohibition against using alcohol, being under the influence, or having detected alcohol presence while on duty, operating, or in physical control.
C0002 fully retains the prohibition on possessing qualifying wine, beer, or distilled spirits while on duty or operating a commercial motor vehicle.
C0002 explicitly incorporates the shipment manifestation exception.
C0002 explicitly incorporates the exception for alcohol possessed or used by bus passengers.
C0003 fully covers the prohibition on motor carriers requiring or permitting drivers to violate paragraph (a).
C0004 fully covers the prohibition against motor carriers permitting drivers who appear to have used alcohol within the preceding 4 hours to be on duty or operate a CMV.
C0005 fully covers the mandate placing drivers in violation of paragraph (a) or (b) out of service immediately for 24 hours.
C0006 covers the provision defining when the 24-hour out-of-service period commences.
C0007 fully covers the prohibition on violating the terms of an out-of-service order.
C0008 fully covers the duty of a driver to report out-of-service order issuance to their employer within 24 hours.
C0009 fully covers the duty and condition-dependent timelines for reporting out-of-service order issuance to the State licensing official.
Claims C0010, C0011, and C0012 jointly cover the complete administrative review process and petition rights under paragraph (e).
